entities.name: Query protein (337 aa)
observations: Sequence length is 337 aa; predicted molecular weight is 37.3 kDa and theoretical pI is 6.17.
Strongly matches reviewed aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenases at 48.5–57.6% identity and 97.3–97.6% query coverage.
Likely cytosolic homodimeric NADPH-dependent enzyme; exact organism is not established from sequence alone.

entities.name: Aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase
observations: EC 1.2.1.11; catalyzes reductive dephosphorylation of L-aspartyl-4-phosphate to L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde using NADPH.
Curated homologs are annotated as cytosolic homodimers with NADP binding and an active-site acyl-thioester intermediate.
Participates in lysine, methionine, and threonine biosynthesis from aspartate.

entities.name: L-aspartyl-4-phosphate reduction
observations: Reaction: L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde + phosphate + NADP(+) = 4-phospho-L-aspartate + NADPH + H(+), represented in the retrieved evidence as RHEA:24284 with reversible direction notation.
Functional description identifies the physiological direction as NADPH-dependent formation of L-aspartate semialdehyde from L-aspartyl-4-phosphate.

entities.name: Aspartate-family amino acid biosynthesis
observations: Asd supplies L-aspartate semialdehyde, a branch-point intermediate for de novo lysine, methionine, and threonine biosynthesis.
The enzyme is step 2 in the aspartate-to-homoserine route and in the lysine diaminopimelate route.
